name: steve_update
description: Tell Steve (and the user) what you are doing now and your current plan. Call it when you start, and whenever the plan or your current step changes.

now.description: one short sentence, in the user's language

name: steve_ask
description: Ask the user a question you cannot answer yourself. Prefer concrete options. Do not ask in plain text; use this tool, then end your turn.

options.description: 2–4 choices; the user may also answer freely

recommended.description: the option you would pick (one of options)

why.description: one sentence: why you recommend it

name: steve_request_approval
description: Ask the user to approve an action with outside effects before doing it: deploying or releasing, sending a message or email, spending money, deleting data, pushing to a shared branch.

detail.description: exactly what will happen, so the user can decide

name: steve_deliver_file
description: Publish an immutable file version into Hub storage and return a stable preview link (url) after the full transfer succeeds, for the user to open on any device, including a phone through the Hub's public address. Works in any session with a working directory: items, chats, conversations and scheduled runs. Does not end the turn or create a public share. Use a file inside this session directory (or, in an item, its outputs directory); ZIP a folder first. entrypoint optionally selects the file a ZIP opens to (an HTML page, a Markdown document, a PDF...). The page previews HTML, Markdown with relative package images, PDF, images, audio, video and text/code. HTML is static (scripts off) unless interactive is true: then the page runs the package's scripts in an isolated sandbox with no access to Steve, cookies or storage and no network beyond package files; inline and package scripts and styles work, external CDNs and fetch do not, so bundle every asset. In an item, preserve the returned url including its ws query in steve_deliver outputs to associate the delivery card. Check access_warning for local-only addresses and unverified reachability.

path.description: Actual file path on this session Node.

entrypoint.description: File a ZIP opens to, e.g. design/index.html or docs/README.md.

interactive.description: Run the HTML's scripts in the isolated interactive preview (prototypes with tabs, state switchers, theme toggles). Default false: static.

name: steve_deliver
description: Deliver the finished work for the user's acceptance. Include what you produced and the checks you ran. Then end your turn.

summary.description: what was done and how it was verified, in the user's language

kind.description: e.g. branch, commit, PR, file, document

role.description: result (default): what the goal asked for. record: evidence of the work, not the result itself, such as self-check screenshots, logs, test reports or intermediate files; the item shows them in its work record instead of its outputs

outputs.description: the final deliverables; a newer delivery replaces the outputs of an earlier one, so list everything that is still current

operated.description: true when you actually used the running thing yourself (opened the page and clicked through, ran the upgrade, called the live API), not a build or a test; name the check with what you saw

scope.description: unit (default): check for your changed scope that must pass. baseline: pre-existing unrelated check failure already present on the base commit. external: live third-party/provider outage outside repository control

checks.description: build, tests, manual checks you actually ran

unfinished.description: plan steps (exact text) you deliberately left open; they and any step not ticked off are shown to the user as left open. A collaboration work unit cannot deliver with open steps

name: steve_publish
description: Ask the user to run the project's release action from your branch, after the item was accepted. Only for a project with a release action of its own; in a project finished when its pull request merges, do not call it: push your branch and open the pull request before steve_deliver, and Steve follows the pull request after the acceptance. Then end your turn; the result arrives later.

branch.description: the git branch to release, e.g. steve/st-12

summary.description: what changes for the user, in Chinese
